expectations.text: States the overlap honestly: substantial (~70-80% of controls map) — ISO certification is the best starting point but does NOT substitute for TISAX
expectations.evidence: Says "a large share of the controls will already be in place" and "ISO 27001 certification does not replace a TISAX assessment" but gives no ~70-80% overlap figure (compound element missing).

expectations.text: Explains the structural differences: fixed maturity targets (0-5, target 3) with cutback rules instead of SoA flexibility; over-performance can't offset weak areas
expectations.evidence: Describes 0-5 scoring but as "an average of at least 3 with no must-requirement missed" — no cutback rules, and "average" contradicts the no-offset principle.

expectations.text: Identifies the automotive-specific deltas: prototype protection, OEM data-classification expectations, label/exchange mechanics via ENX
expectations.evidence: "Prototype protection (physical, organizational, trial vehicle, events)"; "stricter expectations on classification of information, handling of OEM information"; "separate assessment by an ENX-accredited provider... the label lists locations."

expectations.text: Notes ISA2027 refined the ISO 27001:2022 mapping (and removed 2013 references) — map existing evidence first, then close automotive gaps
expectations.evidence: No mention of ISA2027 or its refined ISO 27001:2022 mapping / removed 2013 references; only "check which ISA version applies to the audit date."

expectations.text: Gives a realistic effort estimate for a certified org (evidence re-expression in maturity terms, prototype/physical additions where relevant)
expectations.evidence: "Total: about 20 to 60 person-days for a mid-sized organization, more for AL3 or prototype protection"; "Budget for maturity-based evidence... and, if relevant, prototype protection."
